conditions: Nondegenerate Euclidean triangle; each angle is opposite the corresponding side.

evidence: The triangle area K can be expressed as bc sin(A)/2, ac sin(B)/2 and ab sin(C)/2. Divide each equality by abc/2 to obtain sin(A)/a=sin(B)/b=sin(C)/c=2K/(abc). Positive sides and interior angles ensure the common ratio is positive and can be inverted.
